narrative.overview: A soft, warmly-lit ledger of your progress. The page is a faint rose-tinted off-white; content lives on crisp white cards that lift cleanly off it. One deep-rose accent carries everything that means forward motion — progress fills, scores, the primary action. Restrained in the Linear tradition, but warm rather than clinical. Light-first, with a rose-accented warm-charcoal dark theme as a genuine peer; both meet WCAG AA. It rejects the corporate-LMS look and cheesy gamification: progress is shown honestly, never performed.
keyCharacteristics: Faint rose page + white cards; a single deep-rose accent for progress & action.
Disciplined semantics: rose = progress/success, amber = below the line, blue = booked exam, gray = queued/mid.
Light-first, with a rose-accented warm-charcoal dark theme. Both WCAG AA.
Single humanist sans (Figtree), weight for hierarchy, tabular figures.

rules.name: The One Warm Signal Rule
rules.body: Rose means progress and forward motion — and only that. If something rose isn't about progress or the primary action, it's wrong.

rules.name: The Amber-Not-Rose Rule
rules.body: "Needs work" is always amber, never rose. Since rose reads as success here, a weak area in rose would invert the meaning.

rules.name: The White-Card Rule
rules.body: Content sits on white cards, not on the rose page. The page tint is atmosphere; legible content lives on white.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Figtree carries the whole interface. Hierarchy comes from weight, size, and space — never from pairing a second similar sans.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: Layering is done with tone (white card on rose page), not with heavy shadows. Any shadow that appears is a response to state.

dos: Do reserve rose for progress, success, and the single primary action.
Do flag "needs work" in amber, never rose.
Do keep content on white cards; let the rose page stay atmosphere.
Do hold both light and dark themes to WCAG AA.
Do pair every status with an icon + label; cap body measure at 65–75ch; give every interactive element a visible focus ring.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion alternative for every transition.
donts: Don't make it look like a corporate LMS / compliance dashboard.
Don't use cheesy gamification — no confetti, mascots, XP theatrics, or badge walls.
Don't tint content cards pink — rose belongs to the page and the accent.
Don't pair two similar sans-serifs; one humanist family, varied by weight.
Don't add tiny all-caps tracked eyebrows, or use color as the only signal for status.
Don't spread the rose onto non-progress decoration.
